g.metadata: {"proof": "Theorem26;Exercise26", "strict_naturality": "X_theta S_Fprime = S_F Y_theta", "projection": "Qhat=Q0(1+delta H0)^-1", "section": "unchanged S0", "target_diagram": "unchanged original Y", "parameter_series_bound": "r+1 summands", "Y_basis_degrees": {"y": 0, "z": -1}, "acyclic_pairs": {"f(-1)": "g(0)", "u(0)": "v(1)"}, "N": {"f": "z", "u": "g"}, "X_t_power": "Id+mN", "Y_t_power": "Id", "first_core": "Qhat(st^a;g)=-az", "second_core": "Qhat(st^a|st^b;v)=abz", "truncation_defect": "6z for a=2,b=3 on u", "free_background": "https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/9910179#page=13"}
g.text: The outer comparison keeps its target fixed
Actual full graph actions · the strict natural section
X_θ S_F′ = S_F Y_θ
δ_X S₀ = S₀ δ_Y H₀ S₀ = 0
Q̂ = Q₀ (1 + δ_X H₀)⁻¹
The section stays S₀; the target stays the original Y.
Q₀ δ_X S₀ = δ_Y
At outer parameter length r: at most r + 1 summands.
A strict dg diagram with two adjacent acyclic pairs
Y = k y⁰ ⊕ k z⁻¹
f⁻¹ → g⁰ u⁰ → v¹
H(g) = f H(v) = u N(f) = z N(u) = g
X(tᵐ) = 1 + mN Y(tᵐ) = 1 N² = 0
The original positive parameters remain distinct.
The second parameter term is essential
Q̂_core(stᵃ ; g) = −a z
v → u → u + b g → b f → b f + ab z
Q̂_core(stᵃ | stᵇ ; v) = ab z
With a = 2 and b = 3, omitting that second core gives
(D_Y Q̂≤₁ − Q̂≤₁ D_X)(st² | st³ ⊗ u)
All target parameter images were ordinary identities.
Full series and signs: Theorem 26. Exact diagram: Exercise 26.
Free module background: Keller, arXiv:math/9910179, §4.2.
Joint unit normalization is proved separately in Theorem 27.
